doc.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Segregation and jazz culture
summary: Domber says segregated society and black power shaped the music's evolution.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I think, were you saying that — someone this morning was talking about — maybe it was Jim Cullum — that you can’t really separate American culture when you study jazz history. It’s all one and the same.
I think I made that comment.

But others might have made the same thing. Yeah it’s true, it’s true. You can look at, I’ve always felt that our segregated society had a lot to do with the music with the evolution of the music during those times. I think also the rise of the black power movement after World War II had a lot to do with the direction that music took at that time. And in that sense the music was really related to the culture and the cultural phenomena that were taking place at the time.
